content:
The New York Times on Tuesday defended its reporter Maggie Haberman after the Trump White House accused her of having a “creepy obsession” with the president.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle lashed out at Haberman after she suggested Donald Trump’s relationship with his former chief of staff, Susie Wiles, had changed following her breast cancer diagnosis in March.

Speaking on the latest episode of Fox News host Jessica Tarlov’s “Raging Moderates” podcast, Haberman said Trump views illness “as weakness” and “so, he started picking on” Wiles.

Wiles announced in September that she was cancer-free. Trump replaced her with hard-liner Stephen Miller following the GOP’s drubbing in the 2026 midterm elections.

Ingle responded in a statement shared by the White House’s rapid response account on X: “Maggie Haberman of the Failing New York Times constantly speaks like she knows President Trump when in reality she just has a creepy obsession with the President and clings onto him for relevance and to make money. It’s been very sad to watch for years.”

The Times’ public relations department hit back, highlighting Haberman’s extensive, years-long experience covering Trump and defending her reporting.

“Maggie Haberman has covered six presidential elections and reported on Donald Trump for the past three decades, long before his first run for president,” it said.

“She is an exemplary journalist whose deeply sourced, consequential reporting has informed millions of Americans about vital decisions made by those in power. This is a tired attempt to belittle a journalist for doing her job, in retaliation for coverage the administration doesn’t like,” it added.

Trump has repeatedly targeted Haberman with personal insults, previously dubbing her “Maggot Haberman” and calling her a “sleazebag.”
